title: Check yourself: Images: sources, limits, cost and the picture Claude actually sees

questions.stem: A review service sends thirty scanned pages, each 3000 pixels wide, in a single call, and the API refuses it with an invalid_request_error that cites a stricter limit for crowded requests. Which repair does the page document?

options.text: Send the pages through Amazon Bedrock, which has no per-image limit at all
options.says: Ruled out because the limits table gives Amazon Bedrock its own cap, "Size of one image, Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud (base64)", so a per-image limit exists there too.

options.text: Raise the output limit so that the reply has room to describe all thirty of them
options.says: Ruled out because the stricter limit is "a stricter per-image dimension limit", which concerns the size of each file and not the reply.

options.text: Convert each page to GIF so that the stricter size limit stops counting it
options.says: Ruled out because "Every `image` block counts" toward the stricter limit, whatever its format.

options.text: Downscale every file until neither side is longer than 2000 px, keeping all of them together
options.says: The page says to resize each image "so that neither dimension exceeds 2000 px, or keep the request to 20 or fewer image and document blocks."

origin.section: Limits that end in an error

questions.stem: A scanned A4 page is 1075 by 1520 pixels, both sides under the 1568 edge limit. On a standard-tier model, Claude points at (462, 654) for the signature line, yet the click lands above and to the left of the line on the original. What explains the miss?

options.text: The picture it viewed was 924 by 1307, so every returned value needs rescaling by that size
options.says: The page works the example: 1075 by 1520 costs 2145 tokens, so on the standard tier it "is resized to 924 by 1307" and the point is in that picture.

options.text: The reply was normalized to a 0 to 1000 grid and was then used as plain pixels
options.says: Ruled out because "Claude does not work well when you ask for normalized coordinates", and it returns pixel positions.

options.text: Claude pads every image on the top and left, which moved the origin downward
options.says: Ruled out because the padding sits "on the bottom and right", so the origin does not move.

options.text: Pictures under the edge limit are returned untouched, so the model misjudged the line
options.says: Ruled out because "The token limit can resize an image whose sides are both under the edge limit."

origin.section: The size Claude saw, and why coordinates depend on it

questions.stem: A support agent keeps ten screenshots in a long chat and attaches all of them as base64 on every turn. Latency climbs with each turn. What does the page recommend?

options.text: Re-encode them as heavily compressed JPEG until the payload shrinks to a few hundred kilobytes
options.says: Ruled out because "Lossy compression can add artifacts that hurt text".

options.text: Move to a model with a larger window, which makes the repeated bytes cost nothing
options.says: Ruled out because the problem is that "each request resends the full conversation history", whatever the window size.

options.text: Upload each one once and refer to it by id, so the payload stays small
options.says: The page says that an uploaded file keeps the payload small "regardless of how many images accumulate in the conversation history."

options.text: Place the screenshots after the text, because that order shortens the transfer
options.says: Ruled out because the placement advice is only that Claude "works best when images come before text".

origin.section: Three ways to send an image
